children: Around a fifth of global refineries are at risk of closure as they face falling or negative operating net cash margins over the coming years, according to a report from oil analyst group Wood Mackenzie. The current exceptional margins will fade and return to more modest levels, the report notes. The future for the refineries is complicated because they generate lower returns on capital than upstream operations, it says. This makes securing the capital for upgrades and adaptation hard to achieve, the report says. "For investors and asset owners, the question is not whether a refinery will face pressure, but whether its archetype, location and ownership structure give it the tools to adapt," the report says. (adam.whittaker@wsj.com)
